speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (likely exacerbated by inadequate intake/failure to thrive).

The mention of your brother dying from liver issues and the suggestion of appendicitis are not consistent with a newborn's presentation of jaundice; appendicitis is extremely rare in this age group and does not present primarily as yellow discoloration. Given the history of exclusive breastfeeding, we must rule out dehydration and insufficient milk intake. Have you noticed the baby has fewer than 6 wet diapers per day or has not had a bowel movement in the last 24 hours?
